title: Hospital Website Architecture: Departments, Emergencies and Visitor Information
summary: A hospital website should separate the tasks of getting urgent help, finding a department, identifying a clinician, planning a visit and contacting the institution.
answer: A hospital website should separate the tasks of getting urgent help, finding a department, identifying a clinician, planning a visit and contacting the institution. A single promotional homepage cannot serve all of these needs. The strongest architecture begins with governed department, doctor and location records, then presents clear journeys for emergency and planned-care visitors.

blocks.alt: Hospital website information and visitor routes
blocks.caption: Original Marketing Tusk Healthcare information design model; conceptual illustration.

blocks.text: Build around visitor tasks, not organization charts

A hospital may be organized internally by clinical specialties, administrative departments and business units. Visitors are not required to know that structure. Someone trying to find emergency contact details has a different task from a caregiver looking for visiting hours, an outpatient looking for the correct clinic, or a referring professional checking departmental services.
A useful website separates at least five intentions:

items: **Emergency help:** Accurate urgent contact and arrival information appropriate to the hospital's actual capabilities.
**Find a department:** A browsable directory of genuine services with verified location context.
**Find a clinician:** Factual profiles linked to real departments and current affiliations.
**Plan a visit:** Address, transport, entrances, accessibility, timing and practical requirements.
**Administrative enquiry:** Appointments, records requests or institutional contact through suitable workflows.

blocks.text: The site should not attempt clinical triage through an unverified chatbot or suggest a treatment choice to visitors. A clear digital pathway helps users reach the responsible operational team; clinical decisions remain with qualified professionals.
Separate emergency from routine outpatient routes

**Emergency information needs its own persistent, immediately recognizable route.** Do not force visitors to navigate an outpatient appointment funnel to find a staffed emergency contact or entrance. Show only verified capabilities, telephone numbers, department hours, directions and any official emergency instructions authorized by the institution.

A hospital may have a dedicated emergency department, limited hours in a certain facility, or separate ambulance arrangements. These are not interchangeable. A digital team must obtain the correct operational facts from the emergency/administrative owner, confirm them regularly and avoid claims such as “24-hour emergency” unless the service is actually offered as described.
Table: Visitor task / Primary information / Important design safeguard

items: Visitor task: Urgent help; Primary information: Confirmed emergency contact and arrival instructions; Important design safeguard: Never rely only on an inbox or unmonitored form
Visitor task: OPD appointment; Primary information: Department, location, hours, administrative booking path; Important design safeguard: Never present an enquiry as a confirmed appointment
Visitor task: Diagnostic visit; Primary information: Actual facility, preparation guidance if clinically approved; Important design safeguard: Avoid generic instructions for every test
Visitor task: Visiting a patient; Primary information: Visiting policy, location and contacts; Important design safeguard: Review for currency and privacy
Visitor task: Records enquiry; Primary information: Appropriate authorized contact and secure process; Important design safeguard: Do not expose patient identifiers publicly

blocks.text: Place relevant emergency instructions where visitors are likely to seek them, including the header or contact route where appropriate. Red color alone is not sufficient: use descriptive text and clear affordances. If official local emergency services are referenced, verify them against current government sources before publication.
Treat the department directory as structured data

Each department needs a governed record with: public name, approved description, hospital building and floor or branch where applicable, contact channel, opening/consultation information, related clinicians and links to appropriate informational pages. Some departments operate in more than one location; a directory should reflect that reality rather than imply every service is available everywhere.
A department page can contain:

items: The department's purpose and the institutionally approved service scope.
Where it operates and how to reach the correct entrance or help desk.
Accurate clinician or team affiliations, where these are publicly listed.
Administrative consultation or enquiry arrangements.
Visitor logistics and information relevant to the department.
Links to appropriately reviewed educational material, when useful.
A source-owner and review record held internally.

blocks.text: Avoid filling the page with unverified “advanced treatment” and “world-class outcome” language. For medical institutions in India, the [NMC's October 2026 guidelines](https://nmc.org.in/whats-new/download/1874) should be reviewed when preparing public institutional information and promotional content. They require accuracy and contain restrictions on misleading claims and patient solicitation; final legal interpretation depends on the institution and applicable laws.
A sample website taxonomy
**Home → Departments → Department detail → Doctors / location → Administrative appointment.**

A parallel route should be **Home → Emergency and urgent contact → Verified emergency information**. A third may be **Home → Plan your visit → Maps, accessibility, visitor policies and contact**. These routes should share consistent header navigation but not collapse into one generic form.
Link clinicians to real departments and places

Doctor directories often become unreliable when biographies are copied across locations and availability is maintained separately in spreadsheets. Instead, store clinician identity, verified qualifications, professional designation, department affiliations and actual practice locations as linked records.

The public template may show a concise profile and a safe administrative appointment option. Editorial staff should never create unapproved credentials, ranking claims or “most successful specialist” labels. A review owner should confirm changes when a clinician changes their schedule or department.

The CMS data model can use **Department ID → Clinician ID → Location ID → Appointment route**, allowing one update to propagate to authorized pages. Location and clinician records should include their last-confirmed timestamps internally even if that operational detail is not displayed publicly.
Put visitor logistics into ordinary web text

A hospital's website may contain extensive PDF brochures, maps, circulars and visiting-time posters. These can be useful supporting files, but they should not be the only places where basic visitor information exists. Publish practical information as readable web content with clear headings, links and meaningful alternatives to complex images.

A visitor page should address, where relevant: exact address and campus/building identity, parking or public transport information, entrance directions, accessibility information, visiting hours, visitor contact points, permitted items or policies and how policy changes are communicated.

Do not invent wheelchair access or mobility assistance claims because the hospital is expected to have them. Any statement about on-site facilities must be verified by the appropriate operations team. Where maps are used, provide text instructions that remain meaningful without the map.
Design multilingual navigation around real tasks

Language localization should begin with the most important visitor tasks, not a machine-translated pile of SEO pages. Prioritize labels, contact routes, addresses, directions, visiting rules and appointment instructions for languages that the institution can accurately maintain. Keep contact numbers and branch names consistent across language versions.

Use qualified translators and, for medically sensitive terms, appropriate clinical reviewers. Avoid changing the meaning of eligibility criteria, policies or procedural instructions. A language switcher should be easy to find and should lead to the equivalent page when that translation exists, not silently return the user to the homepage.

W3C's [WCAG 2.2 reference](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/) and [cognitive usability guidance](https://www.w3.org/TR/coga-usable/) provide useful criteria for readable content, clear navigation and accessible interfaces. HTML language metadata and correctly labelled controls are part of technical implementation, not merely translation quality.
Give every factual page an accountable owner

Many hospital website problems are operations failures disguised as design problems. A department's hours change but the website has no owner; an outdated visiting policy remains linked from search; two emergency contact numbers conflict across pages. Good governance is more important than an elaborate homepage redesign.

Create a **content ownership register** with public page URL, source department, factual owner, clinical reviewer if needed, digital editor, last verification date and next review trigger. Triggers may include a branch opening, staffing change, new facility, revised visitor policy or closure of a department.

For changes affecting urgent contact and emergency information, use an expedited, explicitly authorized update process. Record what changed, who approved it, and which external pages or search listings may also require correction.
Ten-point hospital website review checklist

items: Emergency and routine outpatient routes are visibly separate.
Urgent contact information is accurate, staffed as represented and easy to find.
Departments have current, factual service and location records.
Doctors link to real departments and practice locations without fabricated ranking claims.
Appointment journeys distinguish requests, provisional slots and confirmations.
Branch, building and campus information is unambiguous.
Visiting information is accessible as ordinary web text, not only a graphic.
Multilingual essential information is accurate and maintained in parallel.
Mobile and keyboard visitors can complete high-priority tasks.
Content and operational owners can demonstrate an update and review process.

blocks.text: Do not convert this checklist into a clinical safety rating. It assesses website information and administrative access, not treatment efficacy, licensing or hospital accreditation.
A 30-day website governance sprint

**Days 1–7: Inventory critical pages.** Locate every emergency, department, doctor, address, visiting policy and booking page. Assign operational owners. Fix any conflicting critical contact information only after confirmation.
**Days 8–14: Normalize records.** Build standardized department, clinician and campus fields. Identify where current CMS templates duplicate facts, and define the approved information hierarchy.

**Days 15–21: Test visitor journeys.** Use real-world scenarios with synthetic data, including emergency information discovery, OPD appointment navigation and finding visitor hours on a phone. Test keyboard access and enlarged text.

**Days 22–30: Establish publishing controls.** Implement owner verification, clinical and legal review when needed, change tracking and regular content freshness checks. Track issues resolved and recurrent errors without collecting patient records in public analytics.

title: How should child therapy websites organize programme information?
summary: Use one service directory and a consistent page template for each genuine programme.
answer: Use one service directory and a consistent page template for each genuine programme. Each programme page should explain the service in plain language, identify the professional roles involved, state where it is available and show how caregivers can make an initial enquiry. Do not build separate pages merely by swapping condition names.

blocks.text: A practical structure

Start with a **Programmes and Services** page, organized by real service categories such as speech-language therapy, occupational therapy and other disciplines actually offered by the centre. Provide a short description and a clear link to each relevant detail page.

Each detail page should use a stable order: what the centre offers; who provides it; applicable age or location information; the assessment or administrative intake process; where appointments take place; and how to contact the appropriate team. Clinicians should approve any descriptions that imply a treatment approach, eligibility or expected outcome.

Avoid jargon-heavy headings and unsupported results claims. A caregiver may not know the precise therapy category before speaking to a professional; the website should explain available services without appearing to diagnose a child. Ask the front desk to review frequent information requests and adjust the directory labels accordingly.

**Owner and review trigger:** The clinical lead approves programme descriptions, while operations confirms actual availability. Recheck pages when a service starts or stops, a clinician changes role, or a branch changes its timetable.

For the complete journey and website checklist, read [Website Usability for Speech, Occupational and Child Therapy Centres](/guides/website-usability-for-speech-occupational-and-child-therapy-centres).

title: What should a speech therapist's profile include?
summary: A speech therapist's website profile should contain the professional's verified name, accurate role, qualifications, relevant registration or professional details where applicable, actual practice location, languages offered if confirmed, and a clear administrative contact route.
answer: A speech therapist's website profile should contain the professional's verified name, accurate role, qualifications, relevant registration or professional details where applicable, actual practice location, languages offered if confirmed, and a clear administrative contact route. Claims about credentials and clinical scope need professional approval.

blocks.text: Essential fields and useful extras

The **essential fields** are identity, professional designation, qualifications presented exactly as verified, and an accurate link to the centre or branch. Where registration information is publicly displayed, ensure the number and authority are represented correctly and kept current.

**Useful optional fields** include spoken languages, service formats offered at that location, appointment coordination arrangements and a short description of areas of work reviewed by the clinical lead. A photograph can help recognition but does not replace credential transparency.

Do not use invented expertise ratings, unsubstantiated success percentages or profiles that suggest a therapist holds a different professional qualification. If a therapist works at two centres, maintain one controlled biography and link it to the real locations rather than publishing conflicting versions.
**Operational owner:** Clinical management verifies professional facts; the digital publisher maintains the webpage. Review the record when qualifications, location, role or availability changes.
For the full profile and navigation framework, see [Child Therapy Website Usability](/guides/website-usability-for-speech-occupational-and-child-therapy-centres).

title: How can a child therapy website help caregivers find contact information?
summary: Put a clearly labelled contact route in the main navigation and on every programme and location page. Display verified phone, email and address information as readable text; offer a short, accessible enquiry form; and say what happens after a request is received.
answer: Put a clearly labelled contact route in the main navigation and on every programme and location page. Display verified phone, email and address information as readable text; offer a short, accessible enquiry form; and say what happens after a request is received.

blocks.text: The simplest contact journey

First, confirm one source of truth for every branch's contact number, address and opening hours. Next, add a **Contact** or **Request a Call** link that remains usable on mobile. From programme pages, direct enquiries to the correct administration team without requiring the caregiver to understand the centre's internal departments.

Avoid forcing visitors into a chatbot or a long form before showing a phone number. A first-contact form can collect the preferred contact method and branch, with an optional administrative question. Discourage sharing detailed information about a child until the centre provides an appropriate, secure intake route.
Provide clear field labels and useful error messages. An acknowledgement should indicate a realistic next step, without making an unverified response-time guarantee.

**Owner and review trigger:** Operations confirms contact details and the digital team tests links monthly or after any branch or phone-system change. Test the journey by asking someone unfamiliar with the site to reach the correct branch in under a few navigational steps; measure whether they find it, not merely how quickly they click.

title: What should a counselling centre website say about confidentiality?
summary: A counselling centre website should explain who handles initial enquiries, why contact information is requested, how it will be used, where visitors can read the privacy notice, and what the centre's communication limits are.
answer: A counselling centre website should explain who handles initial enquiries, why contact information is requested, how it will be used, where visitors can read the privacy notice, and what the centre's communication limits are. It should not promise absolute secrecy or anonymity unless those claims are accurate and legally supportable.

blocks.text: A factual information pattern

A brief notice beside the contact form can state that submissions are handled by an authorized administrative team for appointment coordination and provide a link to the full privacy notice. The full notice should identify the operator and describe the actual collection and processing arrangements in terms reviewed by a privacy professional.

Keep **routine website contact** distinct from **clinical confidentiality during treatment**. They may involve different staff, records and professional responsibilities. Never imply that only a named therapist sees an enquiry if it also passes through an administrator, CRM or third-party provider.

The privacy team should check whether confirmation emails, analytics platforms and messaging tools create further disclosures. For Indian services, applicability of the [DPDP Act](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/Digital-Personal-Data-Protection-Act-2023.pdf) and its phased commencement needs legal review alongside other confidentiality duties.

**Owner:** The data/privacy lead approves the notice and process description; the editor ensures the page text matches it. Review whenever the form, processor, record-retention policy or communication workflow changes.
For design examples, read [Building a Privacy-Conscious Counselling Website](/guides/building-a-privacy-conscious-website-for-counselling-and-mental-health-centres).

title: How can a mental health enquiry form limit sensitive questions?
summary: Use a short administrative form instead of a clinical history questionnaire.
answer: Use a short administrative form instead of a clinical history questionnaire. Start with a name or preferred form of address, one contact channel, consultation format or location preference, and an optional non-clinical question. Reserve symptoms, diagnoses and treatment history for an approved clinical intake process.

blocks.text: Reduce fields in three steps

**First, map every field to a clear purpose.** If a field is not required to arrange an initial conversation, remove it or move it to a later authorized stage. For example, a detailed “Tell us your condition” prompt is rarely necessary to confirm a preferred callback method.

**Second, separate systems.** The marketing website's form should not automatically populate ad-platform audiences, analytics events or shared spreadsheets with mental-health details. Document the permitted data path, role permissions, retention and notification process.

**Third, test the message and errors.** Make labels visible and instructions clear. A neutral confirmation such as “Your request has been received” can avoid repeating a sensitive service selection in a shared inbox. Do not promise a crisis response through an unmonitored contact route.
The centre's clinical operations and privacy leads should approve the workflow. Reassess the form when service types, third-party providers or regulations change.

title: How should a counselling website distinguish psychiatrists and therapists?
summary: Label every professional by their accurate, verified designation and qualifications.
answer: Label every professional by their accurate, verified designation and qualifications. Do not list psychiatrists, psychologists, counsellors and other therapy professionals under an interchangeable “doctors” title. Link each person to the services, locations and consultation formats they actually offer.

blocks.text: Design a transparent directory

Use fields for **professional name**, **designation**, **verified qualifications**, **applicable registrations**, **practice location** and **consultation arrangement**. Add a short role description only after the professional and the clinical lead approve it. Where legal scope-of-practice distinctions are described, confirm them with the appropriate qualified reviewer for the jurisdiction.

A filter labelled “Professional role” helps visitors navigate more accurately than vague terms such as “our top experts.” The centre can also organize the directory by real, approved service areas, but should not imply that any visitor can diagnose themselves or select a specific treatment through a website filter.

Do not invent a rating based on patients' mental-health outcomes or fabricate credentials. If a professional holds more than one qualification, list what is verifiable and relevant without stretching the description into an unsupported clinical claim.
**Maintenance:** HR or clinical administration confirms changes; editorial staff update the linked pages and location records. Recheck whenever someone joins, leaves or changes practice arrangement.
See the [Privacy-Conscious Counselling Website Guide](/guides/building-a-privacy-conscious-website-for-counselling-and-mental-health-centres) for the full patient-access context.

title: What accessibility issues matter most on an eye clinic website?
summary: Prioritize readable text and contrast, text resizing, keyboard navigation, visible focus, descriptive links, accessible forms and location information that does not depend on images. Test the actual appointment and contact tasks, not just an automated accessibility score.
answer: Prioritize readable text and contrast, text resizing, keyboard navigation, visible focus, descriptive links, accessible forms and location information that does not depend on images. Test the actual appointment and contact tasks, not just an automated accessibility score.

blocks.text: Begin with the highest-impact barriers

**Small or low-contrast text** can make opening hours, clinic addresses and practitioner details hard to read. Check appropriate WCAG 2.2 criteria for text contrast and resizing. **Unlabelled icons or form controls** can hide the booking path from assistive-technology users. **Keyboard-only failures** can make navigation menus, date pickers or error dialogs impossible to operate.

Also inspect the layout with browser zoom, at mobile screen sizes and with images disabled. Directions and service names must remain understandable as text, not only on a map or graphic. Give links useful labels like “Directions to South Clinic” instead of repeating “Click here.”

A practical test is to start on the homepage, find a named branch, identify a genuine consultation route and reach the contact form without a mouse. Then enlarge text and repeat. Record exact page, issue and recommended fix; a tool score without observable examples is not enough.
**Owner:** Design and engineering repair defects, with an accessibility specialist validating complex behaviors. Recheck after design-system or booking-widget changes.
Read the full [Eye Clinic Accessibility Checklist](/guides/eye-clinic-website-accessibility-and-service-navigation-checklist).

**Reference:** [W3C WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/).

title: How should ophthalmology services be grouped online?
summary: Group services according to the clinic's real, clinically approved departments and visitor tasks.
answer: Group services according to the clinic's real, clinically approved departments and visitor tasks. Show a short directory of the services genuinely offered, then link to pages that identify the responsible team, location, appointment route and carefully reviewed information. Avoid forcing users to choose a treatment themselves.

blocks.text: Use the institution's actual service taxonomy

A hospital with general eye care, retina, cornea, glaucoma and paediatric eye services might present those as top-level groups, **but only if those are real, authorized service lines**. A smaller clinic may need two or three categories, not a sprawling menu copied from a large hospital.

Each group page should link to factual details: what the institution offers, where it is offered, which professionals are associated, and how administrative enquiries work. Procedure explanations should be reviewed by a qualified clinician and should not guarantee a visual outcome.

Avoid creating near-identical SEO landing pages for dozens of eye conditions simply to expand keyword coverage. A few complete, accurate pages are more useful than many shallow pages with conflicting branch information. Link the service group to real clinician and location records in the CMS to keep updates consistent.

**Maintenance trigger:** Review categories when the clinic adds or stops a service, opens a branch or changes clinician affiliations. A clinical lead approves labels; operations validates availability.

title: What should an eye surgeon's online profile contain?
summary: An eye surgeon's public profile should contain their verified name, applicable medical qualifications and registration details, factual specialty and role, actual clinic or hospital affiliations, and correct consultation locations.
answer: An eye surgeon's public profile should contain their verified name, applicable medical qualifications and registration details, factual specialty and role, actual clinic or hospital affiliations, and correct consultation locations. The information should be approved and kept current rather than padded with outcome promises.

blocks.text: Separate identity from promotion

Start with the facts a visitor needs to identify the professional. State the institution's approved professional designation, qualifications as verified, relevant training information if substantively useful, and how a visitor can find the correct clinic. If a doctor works across several branches, connect one authoritative profile to each real location instead of maintaining conflicting biographies.

Optional details might include languages used in consultations, professional memberships or research activity, but these should be verifiable and relevant. Avoid unexplained ranking badges, claimed cure percentages or endorsements that imply guaranteed surgical success.

**Operational requirement:** Clinical administration or the doctor's office confirms identity and location information. The public-facing medical content and any promotional implications require appropriate professional review. Under the [NMC's 2026 guidelines](https://nmc.org.in/whats-new/download/1874), factual communications and medical promotion are not interchangeable.
Update the record whenever a doctor changes professional role, schedule, branch or consultation route, and keep an approval record for material revisions.

title: What belongs on a hospital department page?
summary: A hospital department page should identify the department, describe its actual approved services, show where it operates, link to relevant clinicians, explain administrative appointment routes and provide current visitor contact information.
answer: A hospital department page should identify the department, describe its actual approved services, show where it operates, link to relevant clinicians, explain administrative appointment routes and provide current visitor contact information. Each factual element needs a responsible source owner.

blocks.text: A useful departmental page template

Place the **department name and scope** first. Then include the campus, building or branch where visitors should go, the relevant phone or administrative contact, and verified service availability. Link to a clinician directory filtered for the department if that relationship is accurate and maintained.

Where the department publishes information about procedures, indications, risks or outcomes, use a qualified clinical reviewer. Do not confuse a treatment information page with an invitation to choose treatment without professional assessment.
Provide visitor details, such as how to reach the department or find the correct reception desk, in accessible web text. Avoid making a scanned PDF the only source for essential directions or hours.

**CMS governance:** Department, location and clinician records should be linked, with an assigned editor and operational approver. Recheck the page after staffing changes, facility moves, scheduling changes and policy updates.

For full routing examples, read [Hospital Website Architecture: Departments, Emergencies and Visitor Information](/guides/hospital-website-architecture-departments-emergencies-and-visitor-information).

title: How should hospital websites separate emergency and outpatient information?
summary: Give emergency information a distinct, immediately visible route with verified urgent contact and arrival details.
answer: Give emergency information a distinct, immediately visible route with verified urgent contact and arrival details. Put outpatient appointments on a separate journey that explains departments, consultation locations and administrative booking steps. Never send an urgent visitor through an unmonitored online enquiry form.

blocks.text: Two different information journeys

**Emergency route:** Identify the hospital's actual emergency service, its operating arrangements, confirmed contact channels and relevant entrance or arrival information. Only publish emergency claims and numbers verified by hospital operations. A contact-page link labelled “Emergency” should lead to real information rather than a generic marketing page.

**Outpatient route:** Let the visitor find a department or clinician, verify where the appointment takes place and initiate a routine appointment request. Clarify when the form is only a request and when a slot has actually been confirmed.

Do not present a chatbot as an emergency triage tool unless it is specifically governed, staffed and authorized for that purpose. Display high-priority messages as text, not solely with a red icon or banner. Test both pathways on mobile and by keyboard.

**Accountability:** Emergency administration signs off urgent information; outpatient operations owns bookings; the digital team coordinates publication. Trigger an immediate review when numbers, service hours, entrances or emergency capabilities change.

title: How can hospitals improve multilingual visitor navigation?
summary: Translate and maintain high-priority visitor tasks first: emergency contact, directions, departments, appointment instructions and visiting policies. Use clear language choices, accurate page-to-page language switching, and qualified review for medical or safety-critical wording.
answer: Translate and maintain high-priority visitor tasks first: emergency contact, directions, departments, appointment instructions and visiting policies. Use clear language choices, accurate page-to-page language switching, and qualified review for medical or safety-critical wording.

blocks.text: Prioritize information that people act on

Start with visitor questions, not a blanket instruction to translate every page. Essential navigation items include contact details, campus identity, entrance instructions, visiting hours and forms. Translate key transactional content into languages that the hospital can realistically maintain.

A good language switcher sends users to the equivalent page where available. If that page has not been translated, say so rather than silently redirecting to the homepage. Keep telephone numbers, branch addresses and hours synchronized between languages through a shared underlying record.

Machine translation can assist drafting but should not be the final authority on clinical or emergency terminology. Clinical reviewers and qualified language experts should approve safety-critical information. Ensure the site identifies the language of each page correctly for assistive technologies and keeps forms usable at mobile screen sizes.

**Governance:** Each localized page needs an owner, source-language version and review trigger. When the source department changes a policy, flag all affected translations for update before publishing an inconsistent set.

title: Dermatology Clinic Website Checklist: Credentials, Services and Patient Access
summary: A useful dermatology clinic website should show who provides care, which services are actually available, where they are offered and how an individual can contact the practice.
seoTitle: Dermatology Clinic Website Checklist | Marketing Tusk Healthcare
seoDescription: A factual dermatology website checklist covering clinician credentials, service navigation, branch availability, booking UX and medical claims review.
answer: A useful dermatology clinic website should show who provides care, which services are actually available, where they are offered and how an individual can contact the practice. Clear practitioner credentials, a clinically approved service directory, readable pages and a straightforward appointment route make the website more useful than dramatic outcomes imagery or promotional claims.

blocks.alt: Dermatology website information hierarchy from practitioner credentials to services, branches and contact
blocks.caption: Original Marketing Tusk Healthcare editorial workflow illustration. Conceptual, not a measured clinic audit.

blocks.text: Start with four visitor questions

A visitor may arrive after seeing a practice name, a clinician's profile or a service mentioned elsewhere. The site should answer four questions before asking them to complete a form: **Is this the right establishment? Who will provide the consultation? What is available at my location? How do I contact the team?** These questions define the homepage information architecture.

Do not use a procedure gallery as a substitute for a functioning service directory. A multi-clinic practice can feature **Find a dermatologist**, **Services and facilities**, **Locations**, and **Appointments / contact** as separate first-level routes. If one branch offers a particular service and another does not, the website must say so. A page that treats all services as available at all locations creates avoidable confusion.

A practical information map follows **organization → clinician → approved service category → location → administrative next step**. Content owners should confirm each relationship before publication. The same records can power navigation cards, practitioner pages, branch pages and accessible booking links without repeatedly rewriting facts.
Make clinician profiles factual, useful and maintainable

A practitioner profile should show the professional's preferred public name, qualifications that the practice can substantiate, professionally accurate role or specialty, current consultation location and administrative appointment route. Registration details should be checked against the relevant professional records and the applicable guidance, rather than copied from an old brochure. Avoid treating training attendance, membership and a recognized postgraduate qualification as interchangeable.

Include a short factual description of services within the practitioner's approved professional scope, if relevant. If the clinic has both registered dermatologists and nonmedical aesthetic staff, distinguish their titles and roles. Publishing everyone under an undifferentiated “skin experts” heading undermines clarity about who does what.

**Suggested clinician record:** Display name; approved qualifications; role and specialty; registration information where applicable; verified branch associations; appointment contact; last verification date; responsible approver. The CMS should have one source of truth for each field. A change of location should update the directory and affected branch pages together.

India's [National Medical Commission public communication guidelines](https://nmc.org.in/whats-new/download/1874) distinguish factual institutional and professional information from promotional medical advertising. The precise disclosure and advertising obligations depend on the entity and channel. Obtain a medical-communications review rather than interpreting this website checklist as permission for promotional campaigns.
Organize services without directing people to self-diagnose

Dermatology and skin/laser sites often mix clinical specialties, facilities, branded procedures and aesthetic offerings in one long menu. The solution is a structured taxonomy, not an even longer menu. Start from the practice's verified service inventory and group offerings under short, understandable headings approved by the medical director. These might include **Dermatology consultations**, **Specialist clinical services**, and **Laser or procedural facilities** where those categories are accurate.

Each service page should explain what the institution actually offers, which qualified team or department provides it, the relevant branch, how availability is confirmed and where reviewed educational material can be found. Information about indications, contraindications, side effects, recovery and suitability should be written or approved by a qualified clinical reviewer; it is not safe to generate individualized recommendations from generic website copy.
Table: Required page field / Purpose / Responsible owner

items: Required page field: Approved service name; Purpose: Prevent inconsistent or misleading labels; Responsible owner: Medical director
Required page field: Factual explanation; Purpose: Help the visitor understand the institutional offering; Responsible owner: Clinical reviewer
Required page field: Available location; Purpose: Prevent false branch availability; Responsible owner: Operations manager
Required page field: Relevant clinician or team; Purpose: Show who provides the service; Responsible owner: Clinical administration
Required page field: Appointment route; Purpose: Explain the next administrative step; Responsible owner: Front desk
Required page field: Source and review date; Purpose: Support subsequent updates; Responsible owner: Content editor

blocks.text: Avoid “guaranteed results,” “no risk,” unexplained superiority claims and uncontextualized transformation photography. The [NMC guidelines](https://nmc.org.in/whats-new/download/1874) explicitly address misleading claims and patient testimonials. Consent is not, by itself, a blanket authorization to use clinical patient stories for promotion. Flag such material for qualified review before inclusion in public content.
Design the appointment route as a short administrative task

A visitor should not have to submit sensitive medical details just to ask whether a clinic operates on a particular day. Start with a **Call clinic**, **Find location**, or **Request an appointment** choice. Where a form is used, ask only for information necessary for that administrative request. Do not place diagnosis questionnaires, detailed treatment histories or clinical images inside an ordinary marketing form unless the practice has a legitimate, suitably protected clinical workflow for them.

Appointment buttons should lead to the correct branch and give a clear account of what happens next. If a form merely requests a callback, label it as such instead of promising a confirmed slot. If the clinic cannot offer emergency care, do not visually imply that the website handles urgent medical situations.

Form accessibility is part of this journey. The [W3C form-label guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/) explains why visible, programmatically associated labels help visitors understand and operate fields. Build confirmation messages that do not unnecessarily echo private information into email or shared devices.
Treat mobile clarity and accessibility as core requirements

Test the website on a small screen using realistic tasks: locate a named doctor, find a branch phone number, discover whether a service exists at that branch and complete an enquiry without zooming or hunting for controls. A polished desktop screenshot cannot prove that the booking journey works on a phone.

Use readable body text, meaningful headings, adequate contrast, working keyboard focus, descriptive links and sufficient spacing around buttons. Check whether images have meaningful alternatives, whether labels stay visible when fields are selected, and whether a sticky appointment button obscures the final form field. The [WCAG 2.2 quick reference](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/) provides testable accessibility criteria, but conformance must be assessed for the actual pages, not assumed from a visual checklist.

A useful field exercise is to ask a staff member unfamiliar with the website to complete four tasks in five minutes. Record where they hesitate, which labels they misunderstand, and whether the intended action succeeds. These are observations, not a clinical performance metric.
Put claims and public communications through an approval gate

The most visually persuasive content is not necessarily permissible or trustworthy. Establish a review queue for every page describing professional credentials, outcomes, devices, clinical benefits or comparisons. Keep an approved source for each claim. If a comparison cannot be verified, remove it rather than weakening the caveat.

Separate three approval roles: **clinical accuracy**, **professional/advertising permissibility**, and **digital implementation**. An editor can make a sentence clearer but should not independently decide that a procedure claim is medically supported. A technical publisher can ensure a page is indexed but cannot confer legal approval on its content.

The [Google people-first content guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) emphasizes original usefulness and accurate authorship. It does not reward pages simply for multiplying treatment keywords. Build fewer, better service pages around a real verified offering and a specific user need.
Ten-point dermatology website review

items: The clinic's name, address and contact information match its official records.
Every listed clinician has a factual, current professional profile.
Medical and nonmedical staff roles are clearly distinguished.
The service taxonomy reflects approved offerings rather than keyword lists.
Each service is associated only with branches that actually provide it.
Medical or device claims have source evidence and appropriate review.
No patient images, testimonials or before-and-after promotional claims are included without an applicable permissibility review.
A mobile visitor can reach the correct branch in a few clear steps.
Appointment forms minimize unnecessary sensitive information and have visible labels.
The CMS records content owners, verification dates and publication approvals.

blocks.text: A failed check should lead to a documented, specific improvement. It is not evidence that the clinic provides poor medical care.
A practical 30-day implementation sequence
**Week 1: Inventory.** Export service pages, clinician records, branch information, old brochures and current contact routes. Mark the owner of each fact and record discrepancies.
**Week 2: Restructure.** Approve the service taxonomy, define the clinician and branch fields, and build navigation prototypes. Test the four visitor tasks before redesigning decorative elements.
**Week 3: Implement.** Update the main pages, link services to relevant branches, repair contact routes and improve form usability. Keep medically sensitive copy in review.

**Week 4: Validate.** Run mobile and keyboard checks, verify every clinic location and source, complete the sector review and assign a recurring content owner. Record what changed, rather than claiming better outcomes without measurements.

**References:** [NMC guidelines, 6 October 2026](https://nmc.org.in/whats-new/download/1874); [W3C WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/); [W3C form labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/); [Google people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content).
Questions and answers
What should a dermatologist's professional profile show online?

A dermatologist's professional profile should identify the clinician by their actual professional name, verified qualifications, role or specialization, relevant registration information, current consultation locations and an accurate administrative contact route. These are factual identifiers, not a platform for outcome promises.
How should laser and skin-care information be grouped on a clinic website?

Group laser and skin-care information around the clinic's actual, medically approved services, not an exhaustive list of conditions or fashionable procedure terms. The service hierarchy should separate general dermatology consultation, specialist services and laser or procedural facilities where those categories accurately describe the practice.

title: Keeping Dental Practice Listings Accurate Across Search and Maps
summary: Accurate dental practice listings depend on a verified business name, real operating location, correct phone number, suitable business category and current hours.
seoTitle: Dental Practice Listings Across Google & Maps | MT Healthcare
seoDescription: Keep dental practice names, hours, branches and practitioner profiles accurate across Search and Maps, with owner-authorized updates and ethics checks.
answer: Accurate dental practice listings depend on a verified business name, real operating location, correct phone number, suitable business category and current hours. Keep one internal source of truth, make owner-authorized updates to the relevant profiles, and check that the practice website and Search/Maps continue to agree. Do not create duplicate locations or add keywords to a business name for visibility.

blocks.alt: Dental practice location information control map from verified records to website, Maps and monitoring
blocks.caption: Original Marketing Tusk Healthcare editorial workflow illustration. Conceptual, not a measured clinic audit.

blocks.text: Why listing accuracy is a governance problem

A dental clinic may appear in its own website footer, contact page, map pin, Google Business Profile, appointment provider, directory listings and staff profiles. If each record is edited independently, a branch relocation or change of working hours can leave visitors with conflicting directions. This is primarily an **information-management failure**, not a problem solved by writing more promotional posts.

Treat the official practice record as the system of record. A clinic owner or authorized administrator should verify the real-world business name, address, exact entrance if needed, active telephone contact, regular hours, exception hours, website URL and the person responsible for updates. Publish those facts to each approved destination and keep a change log.

Google's [guidelines for representing a business](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177) require real-world name consistency, precise addresses and appropriate location representation. Their rules also cover separate practitioners, chains and departments. The aim is faithful information, not manipulating search results with added neighborhood keywords or duplicate profiles.
Build a branch-level source-of-truth record
The control record should be detailed enough to resolve conflicting published facts. A practical set of fields is shown below.
Table: Field / Authoritative input / Why it matters

items: Field: Practice trading name; Authoritative input: Signage and approved organizational records; Why it matters: Prevent invented keywords and conflicting names
Field: Branch address; Authoritative input: Verified premises and visitor entrance; Why it matters: Keep directions and contact pages accurate
Field: Main public telephone; Authoritative input: Phone line verified by reception; Why it matters: Reduce misdirected calls
Field: Regular and special hours; Authoritative input: Approved desk schedule; Why it matters: Avoid closed-clinic visits
Field: Primary category; Authoritative input: Actual business activity; Why it matters: Describe the practice accurately
Field: Official branch URL; Authoritative input: Maintained branch page; Why it matters: Connect profile to the correct location
Field: Practitioner relationships; Authoritative input: Current consultation rosters; Why it matters: Avoid outdated doctor/branch associations
Field: Last checked and owner; Authoritative input: Named operational approver; Why it matters: Establish accountability

blocks.text: A central spreadsheet can work for one or two branches if edit permissions and ownership are controlled. Larger dental groups should keep these fields in a centrally managed CMS or location-information service. Do not let unreviewed third-party agents overwrite clinic information without consent.
Make profile ownership and agency permissions explicit

Google's [Business Profile third-party policy](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7353941?hl=en) states that authorized agencies must communicate changes, obtain the owner's consent and preserve the client's ownership or co-ownership. A clinic should generally invite an agency as a manager rather than surrender ownership. Agencies must also disclose that the underlying Google Business Profile service itself is free, separate from agency management fees.

Before editing, record the actual account owner, the authorized manager, the location covered and the intended change. Use the account's supported management workflow, not shared passwords. If access cannot be confirmed, a public audit may identify discrepancies, but it must not claim that a profile has already been corrected.

A practical approval message includes the current publicly visible value, the verified replacement value, the affected branch, who approved it and the date. After implementation, verify the published result. Some changes may undergo platform review, so **submitted** is not always the same as **visible**.
Understand branches versus individual dentists

A dental group operating at genuinely different, staffed locations may need location-specific business records. Each branch should represent a real practice site and should not be created as a separate profile simply to cover more search terms. Google's [location, practitioner and department rules](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177) provide the actual eligibility conditions.

Individual practitioners may qualify for separate profiles when they are genuinely public-facing and directly contactable at the verified location during stated hours. That does not justify a different profile for every specialty or service of one dentist. For a multi-dentist location, Google's instructions distinguish the organization's profile from eligible practitioners' profiles. For a solo practitioner associated with a branded practice, a different configuration may be advised. Apply the correct rule to the real establishment rather than copying a competitor's profile structure.

**Decision sequence:** (1) Confirm the physical location exists; (2) identify the legal/trading business; (3) confirm staff and patient-facing presence; (4) establish whether an eligible practitioner record is appropriate; (5) assign owner and managers; (6) publish and inspect for duplication. The practice owner's account should remain the starting point.
Make hours describe the actual service experience

“Open” can mean different things in a dental practice: reception staffed, consultations scheduled, procedures conducted or emergency calls answered. The public business hours should reflect what a visitor can realistically expect, and additional hours or appointment-specific information should be described using available platform fields and factual website copy.

When the practice has an unusual holiday schedule, the person who approves staffing should trigger an information update. Do not assume that generic “Open 24 hours” is defensible because a phone number takes messages overnight. A separate after-hours telephone arrangement should be labelled accurately.

Use a **change event** rather than a quarterly reminder alone: whenever a branch moves, closes temporarily, adds holiday hours, changes number or changes practitioner availability, update all relevant public destinations. Recheck changes after publication and monitor calls to the wrong site as an operational signal.
Keep the website and external surfaces aligned

The practice website should have a clear branch page with official name, precise address, telephone, accessible directions link and verified hours. A central clinic locator can link to these records. Avoid branch pages that contain the same generic treatment copy but omit branch-specific facts.

Inspect representative directories, map services and third-party appointment providers for conflicting details. For external sites outside the clinic's control, document a correction request and follow the platform's legitimate process. Record a link and capture the result once visible. Do not use unauthorized account claims or impersonation to accelerate changes.

Track three operational indicators: **accuracy of critical fields**, **time to publish approved changes**, and **unresolved conflicting records**. These are agency quality metrics, not measurements of clinical care or guarantees of a position in Maps.
Dental ethics: keep listings factual, not solicitational

India's [Revised Dentists (Code of Ethics) Regulations, 2014](https://dciindia.gov.in/Rule_Regulation/Gazette_Notification_reg_DCI_Revised_Dentists_Code_of_Ethics_Regulations_2014_27.06.2014.pdf) address advertising and patient solicitation. The regulations discuss factual dental websites and prohibit misleading or boastful communications. This Guide is about accurate public information, not a prescription for paid patient targeting, generating reviews, creating self-promotional practitioner profiles or putting inducements into a listing.

Avoid fabricated testimonials, misleading ratings, claims of being “best,” and false specialty representations. If a proposed profile edit changes clinical or promotional wording rather than basic operational facts, send it through the practice's dental-ethics review. Google policy compliance and professional ethics are different approval layers; satisfying one does not establish the other.
Ten-point dental listing accuracy checklist

items: Verify the trading name against real-world practice identity and signage.
Maintain one approved record for each actual location.
Confirm addresses, pins, entrances and official website URLs.
Test phone numbers and record who answers each branch line.
Validate regular, special and holiday hours against real staffing.
Use accurate business categories without keyword-stuffed names.
Check practitioner profiles against actual eligibility and consultation arrangements.
Confirm clinic ownership of each managed Business Profile.
Record approvals, submitted corrections and published outcomes separately.
Review external directory conflicts and schedule monitoring after operational changes.

blocks.text: A 30-day correction programme
**Week 1: Establish facts.** Interview the practice administrator, inspect signage and existing branch pages, collect relevant platform URLs and build the verified branch register.

**Week 2: Identify discrepancies.** Compare the register with public Google profiles, maps, contact pages and booking providers. Label observations precisely; do not call a record inaccurate based solely on missing tool access.
**Week 3: Obtain permission and correct.** Have the owner approve the changes. Use authorized manager access and submit updates; store old and new values in a change log.

**Week 4: Confirm and maintain.** Revisit published records, check website links and set an exception-based update workflow for holidays, branch moves and staff changes. Escalate unresolved platform issues using supported channels.

title: Physiotherapy Centre Website and Service Information Checklist
summary: A physiotherapy centre website should explain the services actually offered, identify the practitioners and their verified roles, distinguish clinic and home-visit arrangements, give accurate location/access details, and make contacting the centre straightforward.
seoTitle: Physiotherapy Centre Website Checklist | Marketing Tusk
seoDescription: Plan physiotherapy service pages, factual therapist profiles, in-centre and home-visit information, accessibility and appointment navigation.
answer: A physiotherapy centre website should explain the services actually offered, identify the practitioners and their verified roles, distinguish clinic and home-visit arrangements, give accurate location/access details, and make contacting the centre straightforward. It should help someone understand the administrative pathway without trying to diagnose an injury or promise a recovery timeline.

blocks.alt: Physiotherapy centre website content map from provider and service information to appointment route
blocks.caption: Original Marketing Tusk Healthcare editorial workflow illustration. Conceptual, not a measured clinic audit.

blocks.text: Build around user tasks instead of a long treatment list

Physiotherapy centres often serve visitors who arrive with quite different questions: someone wants to find an existing therapist, someone is checking which branch offers a programme, and someone is arranging a visit for a relative. These are different tasks, even if they ultimately lead to the same reception desk.

An effective first navigation should identify **Services and programmes**, **Therapists and team**, **Location and access**, **Clinic or home visits**, and **Appointments**. A visitor should not have to understand a clinician's internal terminology before locating the right administrative contact.

Don't open with a list of dozens of body parts or conditions merely to capture search queries. A directory needs an approved clinical taxonomy and meaningful explanation of the centre's service categories. Exact programme suitability remains a professional decision. Website copy should never suggest that selecting a link determines a treatment plan.
State therapist qualifications and roles without inflation

A therapist profile should use the professional's actual public name, verified qualification, current role, relevant training where accurately described, services and locations where they work, and an appropriate contact pathway. The practice should verify which professional designations or titles are legally recognized in its jurisdiction rather than inventing a universal credential requirement.

If a centre employs physiotherapists, occupational therapists, assistants and administrative staff, don't present them as interchangeable. A concise “Who is involved” section can explain the difference between a clinician's role and a support role in institution-approved language.
Table: Profile element / Public information / Responsible approver

items: Profile element: Professional name; Public information: Name used in institutional records; Responsible approver: Centre administrator
Profile element: Qualification / role; Public information: Exact verified education and designation; Responsible approver: Clinical director
Profile element: Service involvement; Public information: Approved programmes they support; Responsible approver: Clinical lead
Profile element: Consultation location; Public information: Current branch or home-visit arrangement; Responsible approver: Operations
Profile element: Availability method; Public information: How the visitor can request an appointment; Responsible approver: Front desk
Profile element: Review date; Public information: Last verification and editor; Responsible approver: Publisher

blocks.text: Use a central profile record so a departure, branch transfer or new schedule can be corrected once. Avoid publishing unsupported “highest recovery rate” or similar outcome statistics to fill a thin profile page.
Design a useful service taxonomy

An understandable website does not need to reproduce the centre's entire clinical documentation. It needs a consistent page structure. The exact headings depend on the practice's genuine capabilities: for instance, a centre might distinguish general physiotherapy consultations, sports rehabilitation, neurological rehabilitation, pediatric programmes, postoperative rehabilitation or home-based services **only where those are actually offered and approved**.

For each programme, publish an accessible plain-language overview, the types of appointments the centre provides, who oversees the programme, relevant locations and how to contact staff. Add any clinical discussion about indications, risks, duration or expected progress only after review by an appropriately qualified professional.

A programme page should not diagnose the visitor, tell them which programme to choose or promise a number of sessions needed for recovery. If a clinic cannot verify a claimed outcome, remove that claim. The same goes for images and stories implying that all visitors can expect a particular result.

Link programme pages to the correct branch and therapist relationships. A person should not find a service on the website, complete a form, and learn later that it is not offered at the location chosen.
Clearly separate in-clinic and home-visit services

For many rehabilitation providers, the critical distinction is not clinical but logistical. Can the person visit a facility? Is home-based service offered in their area? Is there an accessibility requirement, building entrance or parking detail they should know? What will the first contact confirm?

A concise availability block can state **In-centre**, **Home visit**, or **Both**, with coverage and scheduling described accurately. A home-visit service area is not the same as a guaranteed promise that every address receives an appointment. Where access depends on staffing or therapist availability, explain that it will be confirmed by the scheduling team.

For a physical centre, publish the actual entrance, address, map link, nearest practical landmark and accessible travel instructions where applicable. If particular equipment or mobility assistance is available, use verified facts. Avoid vague claims such as “fully accessible” unless the actual route has been assessed.

Google's [Business Profile representation guidelines](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177) distinguish storefront businesses, service-area businesses and hybrid services. If the centre manages public profiles, match the listing type to the real operation rather than adding service-area listings for locations that do not exist.
Keep the appointment form administrative

An introductory website form should not become an uncontrolled repository of patient histories. A clinic may need to know a preferred branch, a callback number, a preferred time and the broad appointment type. Detailed diagnoses, prescription images, scans and medical histories should be routed through a secure clinical intake process only when genuinely needed.

Tell the user whether they're requesting a callback or a confirmed appointment. If the centre offers an online booking system, the public page should state how cancellations and rescheduling work and whether the displayed slots are actually available. Do not silently redirect from a named therapist to a generic programme without explanation.

Apply the [W3C form-label guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/): each field should have a meaningful label, required fields should be identified, and errors should be explained in text. Make keyboard focus visible and ensure the form remains usable on a narrow mobile screen. Confirmation messages should avoid unnecessarily exposing sensitive details.
Write for accessible comprehension

A visitor may be managing pain, time pressure, limited mobility or unfamiliar health terminology. The site should reduce effort. Use short sections, descriptive headings, logical tabs, readable text, sufficient color contrast and text links that explain where they lead.

The [WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/) offers concrete accessibility criteria for labels, keyboard access, headings, focus and contrast. A successful accessibility programme combines technical testing with task-based review; passing an automated scanner alone cannot establish conformance.

One practical editorial exercise is to check whether the first paragraph of each service page answers: **What is this service? Where is it provided? How can I ask the centre about access?** Do not force visitors to scroll past promotional imagery for those basic facts.
Assign content owners and build a change process

A website becomes less useful when its content outlives the operating schedule. Common changes include programme names, therapist availability, opening hours, branch moves and home-visit catchments. Each category should have an accountable owner and a defined change trigger.
Table: Change / First approver / Website records to update

items: Change: New therapist; First approver: Clinical lead; Website records to update: Team profile, programme, branch directory
Change: Changed opening hours; First approver: Operations; Website records to update: Branch page, appointment page, public listings
Change: Programme discontinued; First approver: Clinical lead; Website records to update: Service page, navigation, internal links
Change: Home-visit catchment revised; First approver: Scheduling lead; Website records to update: Coverage page, enquiry form, FAQs
Change: Form or booking system changed; First approver: Technical lead; Website records to update: Booking page, confirmation, help text

blocks.text: Keep a dated content log and periodically inspect the site as a first-time visitor. The [Google people-first content guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) prioritizes usefulness and clarity over publishing large numbers of thin service pages.
Ten-point physiotherapy website checklist

items: The centre's identity, locations and contact routes are current.
Practitioner qualifications and roles are factually presented.
Clinical and support-team titles are not conflated.
The service directory reflects the centre's actual capabilities.
Programme pages identify the approved service location and team.
Clinic visits and home visits are clearly distinguished.
Home-visit coverage and availability are not overstated.
Booking forms are legible, labelled and proportionate to an initial enquiry.
Content avoids guaranteed recovery times and unsupported outcome claims.
The CMS has clear owners and procedures for correcting changed schedules.

blocks.text: This checklist measures public information and website experience, not the quality or appropriateness of therapy itself.
A four-week improvement plan
**Week 1:** Inventory programmes, verified therapist roles, locations, access arrangements and intake fields. Record contradictions across the existing website and public listings.
**Week 2:** Create the service taxonomy and reusable therapist/branch templates. Test navigation labels with a small group of staff who did not design the site.
**Week 3:** Implement approved copy, mobile navigation, accessible contact forms and location links. Test the first-contact journey without submitting real patient information.

**Week 4:** Review clinically sensitive wording, confirm all practical details, test accessibility on actual devices and assign owners for service changes. Separate a requested change from a completed change in the signoff log.

Questions and answers
What should a physiotherapy centre website include?

A physiotherapy centre website should include a clear identity and contact page, service and programme overview, truthful therapist profiles, accurate location and accessibility information, and an appointment path that explains what happens after an enquiry. Add home-visit coverage details only if the centre really offers that service.
How should rehabilitation services be grouped online?

Group rehabilitation services according to the centre's real clinical programmes and the visitor's task. A small number of understandable categories is generally more useful than a long alphabetical list of body parts, conditions and techniques.
